title: USB and Peripheral Redirection Failures
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'USB and Peripheral Redirection Failures' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `linux_usb_and_peripheral_redirection_failures` (UC-2.6.39), SOC dashboard panel "Linux — USB and Peripheral Redirection Failures", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:linux_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=xd` sourcetype='citrix:vda:events' that satisfy the UC-2.6.39 SPL filters for 'USB and Peripheral Redirection Failures'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `xd` / `citrix:vda:events` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-2.6.39.

dataSources: `sourcetype="citrix:vda:events"` (USB, TWAIN, WIA, `CtxUsb`, `CtxCam`), `sourcetype="WinEventLog:Application"` for Citrix ICA client driver messages, `index=windows` for Group Policy/clipboard blocks if forwarded; optional `sourcetype="uberAgent:Peripheral:USB*"` if you enable end-point visibility
app: Template for Citrix XenDesktop 7 (TA-XD7-Broker), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows, optional uberAgent UXM (Splunkbase 1448)
spl:
(index=xd sourcetype="citrix:vda:events" OR (index=windows (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Application" OR sourcetype="citrix:vda:events")) OR (index=uberagent sourcetype="uberAgent:Peripheral*"))
| search match(_raw, "(?i)USB|TWAIN|WIA|redirect|peripheral|smart.?card|scard|clipboard|mapped drive|clpb|device.*(fail|deny|block|stop|stall)")
| eval channel=if(match(_raw, "(?i)twain|wia|scan"), "imaging", if(match(_raw, "(?i)clipboard|clip"), "clipboard", if(match(_raw, "(?i)drive|mapped"), "drives", "usb_usb")))
| where match(_raw, "(?i)fail|error|block|deny|policy|restric|not supported|time.?out|stall")
| stats count, values(Message) as sample, earliest(_time) as first_t, latest(_time) as last_t, dc(user) as users by host, channel, user
| sort - count
description: USB, scanner, and smart card redirection, plus client drive mapping and clipboard, depend on VDA services, client versions, and Citrix/Windows policies. Failures are often per-device or per-user but can spike when a new policy, endpoint agent, or firmware change blocks channels. VDA and Application logs capture the denial reason, while optional uberAgent peripheral metrics confirm drop-off in hardware attach success rates.
value: Early 'USB and Peripheral Redirection Failures' detection reduces capacity incidents, patch regressions, and service outages by giving Linux operators a Splunk-native signal before manual triage or audit channels surface the issue.
implementation: Ingest a broad slice of VDA logs with USB/TWAIN categories enabled. Add policy lookup by AD group. Separate Help Desk false positives (unsupported devices) with `NOT match(device_class,"(legacy)")` style filters where fields exist. Correlate with NetScaler/ADC app flow only if the channel is not negotiated locally. Alert on new denial strings in a 24h compare.
visualization: Table (users and channels with sample errors), Pareto chart (error text top 10), Bar chart (failed channel by delivery group if joined).
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Patch Tuesday / unattended-upgrades** — CPU and disk I/O spike during package application for 'USB and Peripheral Redirection Failures'. Correlate with apt/yum logs in same window.

2. **Nightly backup or log-rotate job** — Predictable I/O burst on fixed cron schedule.

3. **Synthetic monitoring probe** — Nagios/Zabbix agent generates periodic load.

4. **New host onboarding** — Baseline metrics unstable first 48h on `xd` `citrix:vda:events`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` keyed on `host`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Template for Citrix XenDesktop 7 (TA-XD7-Broker), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows, optional uberAgent UXM (Splunkbase 1448).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `sourcetype="citrix:vda:events"`, `sourcetype="WinEventLog:Application"`, optional `index=uberagent` peripheral data.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable detailed VDA logging for HDX device redirection per Citrix doc for your LTSR/CR build. If logs are very verbose, route to a dedicated index with shorter retention. Map `user` and `ClientName` fields consistently.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; limit `index=uberagent` to your deployment):

```spl
(index=xd sourcetype="citrix:vda:events" OR (index=windows (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Application" OR sourcetype="citrix:vda:events")) OR (index=uberagent sourcetype="uberAgent:Peripheral*"))
| search match(_raw, "(?i)USB|TWAIN|WIA|redirect|peripheral|smart.?card|scard|clipboard|mapped drive|clpb|device.*(fail|deny|block|stop|stall)")
| eval channel=if(match(_raw, "(?i)twain|wia|scan"), "imaging", if(match(_raw, "(?i)clipboard|clip"), "clipboard", if(match(_raw, "(?i)drive|mapped"), "drives", "usb_usb")))
| where match(_raw, "(?i)fail|error|block|deny|policy|restric|not supported|time.?out|stall")
| stats count, values(Message) as sample, earliest(_time) as first_t, latest(_time) as last_t, dc(user) as users by host, channel, user
| sort - count
```

Step 3 — Validate
Unplug/attach a test USB in lab; confirm a failure path logs if you block via policy. Verify sampling does not include benign detach messages.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Share weekly Top 10 error strings with endpoint engineering. For regulated sites, add privacy guardrails to mask serial numbers in Message.
grandmaExplanation: We look for the hidden notes when a camera, USB stick, or copy-paste path is turned off or breaks inside a remote session — so you catch blocked gadgets before they hurt real work.
